summary: The same Aula sitting on several dates is a suspended-and-resumed sitting, not a source contradiction: the reading is verified against the resoconti archive, and a confirmed one carries `seduta_pluri_giorno: true` plus an authoritative `data_apertura` and keeps its resoconto link. A number the archive does not confirm stays `anomalia: true` without a link, as does the one real contradiction (same date, different sitting numbers). Supersedes the inverse guard added by ars-sicilia-iter-seduta-data-inversa.
reason: That guard fired on 4 budget laws out of 4, across two legislatures - L.R. 1/2019 (sitting 98, 31 Jan -> 15 Feb), L.R. 9/2020 (187, 28 Apr -> 2 May), L.R. 28/2024 (142, 5 -> 7 Nov), L.R. 1/2025 (147, 18 -> 28 Dec) - and suppressed the link on «Approvato dall'Assemblea», the one event a journalist wants to cite. In all four the sitting number is right and the record exists, filed under the opening day: the Assembly opens a sitting, suspends it and resumes it until the budget passes, and the resoconti archive indexes it at the opening date. The original guard's own text anticipated this («una seduta sospesa e ripresa in un altro giorno darebbe la stessa coppia di eventi») but treated it as undecidable. It is not the same case as the twin guard, and the justification for dropping the link does not carry over: there one date holds two different numbers and at least one link would be wrong, here the number is single and resocontoSchedaURL is built from the number, so the link cannot point at the wrong day. Every other Aula event is already linked on the declared number alone, with no verification - suppressing it only here demanded of these events a proof asked of no other. The verification was added after review raised P1 on the first version: without it, `seduta_pluri_giorno` asserts a reconstruction («opened on X, resumed on Y») that the iter alone cannot prove, so a number mistakenly reused on another date would receive that marker, a derived `data_apertura` and a link to an unrelated record - and the marker it replaced (`anomalia`) said something weaker and always true. One request per candidate sitting, and candidates only exist in iters where an Aula number appears on several dates: on the sample, only the budget bills (measured: +1.3s on ddl 733, healthy iters unchanged). A network error does NOT fall back to `anomalia`: a marker that changes with connection quality is worse than one that says it could not verify, so that case keeps the reading and the note says it is unverified.
validated_outcome: `ddl iter 17 476|17 733|18 809|18 832`: all four sittings (98, 187, 142, 147) confirmed by the archive, `data_apertura` in ISO from the archive itself (2019-01-31, 2020-04-28, 2024-11-05, 2024-12-18), no `anomalia`, /bd/resoconti/scheda links present. `ddl iter 17 199`, the genuine same-date/different-number case, still marks its two events and still omits the link. `ddl iter 18 6030` keeps its 6 resoconto links and issues no extra request. esitoVerificaSeduta, the pure rule, is unit-tested on all five outcomes: matching opening date, the same date in two source forms, a sitting the archive does not have (-> anomalia, the case the review raised), a sitting the archive opens elsewhere (-> anomalia), and a failed lookup (-> kept reading, marked unverified). go build, go vet, gofmt, go test ./... green.
